paragraphs: Children and young people in East Ayrshire who cannot live with their birth families are cared for by East Ayrshire Council's fostering and adoption service and by the independent agencies listed on this page. The council looks after children from birth to 18, and its stated aim is that every looked after child in the area gets the same love, support and opportunities as any other.

The council offers short-term fostering, for children whose families are going through a crisis while plans are made, permanent fostering, where a child stays with the same carers into adulthood, intensive fostering, where one child at a time is cared for with a wider support team around them and the carer receives a higher fee, and short breaks that give families a rest. Applicants can be single, married or in a same-sex relationship, working or not, and renting or owning their home. They need to be at least 21 and have a spare room.

East Ayrshire pays each child's allowance at the Scottish Recommended Allowance rates for 2026-27, from £177.68 a week for a child under five to £283.35 for a young person of 16 or over. On top of this it pays a weekly household fee of £280 for one child, £420 for two and £560 for three or more. The council says carers are registered as self-employed and most will not pay tax on their fostering income. Our East Ayrshire allowance page has the details.

The council runs informal local information events for anyone curious about fostering. As agencies set their own fees and support, it is worth comparing the council with one or two of the agencies below before you apply.
